events.title: Release cadence is increasing
events.body: We are moving to twice-weekly releases on the platform. I am telling you rather than asking, but I would rather you heard it from me.

events.title: Nordic market: local payments partner selected
events.body: We have signed a local payments partner for the Nordic entry. Integration work starts next month. I assume there is nothing here that should worry us.

events.title: Cloud migration slips again
events.body:
The migration has slipped another quarter. The remaining legacy workloads are harder than the survey suggested and we have lost two engineers to the platform team.

I know what this does to your legacy exposure. I do not have a better answer today.

events.title: Change freeze for peak trading
events.body: We are entering the peak trading period. Standard change freeze applies to everything touching fulfilment and payments. Security changes are not automatically exempt.

events.title: An enterprise client is asking security questions
events.body: One of the Insight Services clients has sent a 140-question security assessment as part of their renewal. Some of the questions I cannot answer honestly and confidently at the same time.

events.title: Insight Services wants broader data access
events.body: The analytics team want to widen access to the behavioural data lake so more product teams can build on it. Commercially this is the right direction. I am told you may have a view.

events.title: Technology cost review
events.body: Every technology line is being reviewed. I am told your monitoring service is one of the cheaper ones, which is either good news or a question.

events.title: The platform launched
events.body:
We are live. Traffic is ahead of forecast and the first day passed without incident.

Thank you for how you handled the run-up.

events.title: The platform launched, late
events.body:
We are live, later than we told the market. Traffic is ahead of forecast and the first day passed without incident.

Whether the wait is why, neither of us can prove. I have stopped arguing about it.

events.title: The launch is slipping
events.body: The launch is behind. If the date moves, the market will have to be told, and I am not looking for someone to blame, but I am going to want to understand how much of this sits with security conditions.

events.title: Regulator opens a thematic review
events.from: Ruth Ahmadi, General Counsel and Data Protection Officer
events.body: The regulator has opened a thematic review into operational resilience in payment services. We are in scope. They will ask about recovery capability and third-party dependencies.

events.title: An outage, nothing to do with security
events.body: Order management was down for most of the morning. Database failure, no security dimension, but the executive will ask you anyway, because it was an outage.

variants.title: Another outage, still not security
variants.body: Payments were slow for most of the afternoon: a storage fault, nothing malicious. I mention it because somebody on the executive will ask whether it was an attack, and it would help if we gave the same answer.

variants.title: An outage, and the usual question
variants.body: The warehouse systems dropped this morning after a routine change went wrong. No security angle. Expect to be asked anyway.

variants.title: Down, but not attacked
variants.body: Customer sign-in failed for part of the morning because a certificate expired. Not an attack, but the kind of thing an attacker would have enjoyed, and the executive will ask you whether it was one.

events.title: Due diligence window on Kestrel
events.body: There is a window before completion where technical due diligence is still possible. It closes in about six weeks. After that, integration planning takes over.

events.title: The board wants a risk appetite statement
events.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
events.body: The committee has asked for a cyber risk appetite statement. I would like something we could actually test a decision against, rather than three paragraphs about being risk-aware.

events.title: Cyber insurance renewal questionnaire
events.body: The insurers want evidence of multi-factor authentication coverage, privileged access controls and tested backups before they will quote. The questions are specific and they will be checked at claim time.

events.title: Payment volumes up 30%
events.body: Payment volumes are running 30% above forecast. Good news commercially. It also means the payment platform is now carrying more of the business than the resilience assumptions were built on.

events.title: A project you had not heard of
events.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
events.body: The commercial team have been running a customer data enrichment project with an external provider for four months. Nobody told us. The data flows out of the analytics estate nightly.

events.title: A merchant is asking about card data handling
events.from: Ruth Ahmadi, General Counsel and Data Protection Officer
events.body: One of the larger merchants has asked, in writing, for confirmation that card data is not retained outside the payment environment. I would like to answer accurately.

events.title: The CIO wants the security conditions eased
events.body: Two delivery teams have raised that security review is now the longest step in their release process. I am not asking you to drop it. I am asking whether it has to look like this.

effectsOnReveal.concern: Security review time in the release process

events.title: A quiet quarter
events.body: Nothing has gone wrong for three months. I am told that is partly your doing, and partly luck, and that you would be the first to say which is which.

events.title: A competitor has been breached
events.body: One of our competitors has lost customer data and it is on the front page. The board will ask me on Thursday whether it could happen to us. I would like a better answer than 'possibly'.

events.title: The cost of a control nobody uses
events.from: Nadia Farrell, Director of Procurement and Supplier Management
events.body: We were paying for a data classification tool that the last review found deployed to 4% of the estate. Nobody told me it was about to be used, so I have cancelled it, and the £60k comes back to the cyber budget this year.

effectsOnReveal.note: An unused licence has been cancelled.
